column4: The Holy Spirit is not a new spirit but is of God and has been with God since the very beginning. In Genesis 1:2 the Spirit of God is hovering on the waters during creation. In Nehemiah 9:20, the scriptures say that it was the Spirit who instructed the people in the wilderness. It was by this same Holy Spirit that God anointed the kings, judges, and prophets in the Old Testament. In Joel 2:28-29 the Spirit is promised to be poured out on all mankind. It was by this same Holy Spirit that God raised Jesus from the dead, and now dwells in us (Romans 8:11). There is only one Holy Spirit, and He has always been the same. How He works with people has looked different at different times, but His heart has never changed.

column4: In John 20, after His resurrection, Jesus appears to His disciples in the middle of a locked room and breathes on them saying ‘*Receive the Holy Spirit*’ (John 20:22). The theology is somewhat debated on precisely what occurred at that moment, but most Pentecostal interpretations view this as the disciples receiving the Spirit of God inside them, signifying the new birth, being born-again. This was not, however when they received the Spirit of God upon them, empowering them with boldness for ministry. This was when they received the Holy Spirit within them, allowing them to abide and commune with God. This will be discussed at greater depth later in this chapter as well as the chapters on sanctification and baptism.

column4: The Holy Spirit is first and foremost, from and of God. The scriptures refer to the Spirit as the Spirit of God, or the Spirit of the Lord, or the Spirit of Christ, while these highlight different aspects, they are all one in the same. The Holy Spirit, being fully God, is also eternal and is holy (blameless, innocent, pure, not profane). Some translations refer to the Holy Spirit as the Holy Ghost.
column5: The Holy Spirit, first and foremost, comes from God and belongs to God. The Scriptures refer to the Spirit as the Spirit of God, or the Spirit of the Lord, or the Spirit of Christ; though these emphasize different aspects, they are all the same. The Holy Spirit, being fully God, is also eternal and holy (blameless, guiltless, pure, not impure). Other translations refer to the Holy Spirit as “Holy Ghost”.

column4: The word spirit in Greek is ***Pneuma** (NYOO-mah -* **G4151***),* it means breath, or wind. The Hebrew word for spirit means the same. Breath is significant as we need it in constant supply to live. It was God's breath that He blew into Adam to bring Him to life, likewise it was Jesus' breath that He breathed last before He died on the cross. Without breath there is no life. Breath like wind can be felt and experienced but are not as easily observed as other ‘elements’ water, fire, earth.

column4: Diving deeper, the Spirit brings conviction of these three truths:

column4: 1.  **Conviction of sin**: Revealing the reality of human rebellion against God, drawing men’s attention to the depravity of their own lives.
column5: 1.  **Conviction of sin**: Revealing the reality of humanity's rebellion against God, drawing people's attention to the depravity of their own lives.

column4: 2.  **Conviction of righteousness**: Demonstrating Jesus’ perfect fulfillment of the Father’s will, and that Jesus' sacrifice provided the one-time atonement needed for forgiveness of sins.
column5: 2.  **Conviction of righteousness**: Showing the perfect fulfillment of the Father's will accomplished by Jesus, and that Jesus' sacrifice provided the once-for-all atonement needed for the forgiveness of sins.

column4: 3.  **Conviction of judgment**: Affirming the defeat of Satan, the certainty of God’s justice, and that all will stand a judgement for their life's work and deeds.
column5: 3.  **Conviction of judgment**: Affirming the defeat of Satan, the certainty of God's justice, and that all will stand in judgment for the works and deeds of their lives.

column4: The entire book of Acts is full of stories and accounts that have this general cycle:
column5: The entire book of Acts is filled with stories and accounts that generally follow this cycle:

column4: 1.  **Prayer**: Believers ask for boldness and God’s intervention.
column5: 1.  **Prayer**: Believers pray for boldness and God's intervention.

column4: 2.  **Empowerment**: The Holy Spirit fills them with courage, power, and guidance.

column4: 3.  **Proclamation**: They boldly declare the gospel, often with signs and wonders and miracles.

column4: 4.  **Opposition**: Resistance arises, leading to persecution or challenges. Sometimes believers were martyred, other times imprisoned and or beaten.
column5: 4.  **Opposition**: Opposition arises, leading to persecution or challenges. Sometimes believers were killed for their faith, at other times imprisoned and/or beaten.

column4: 5.  **Renewal**: The church returns to prayer, seeking fresh empowerment, and the cycle continues.
column5: 5.  **Renewal**: The church returns to prayer, seeking fresh empowerment, and the cycle continues.

column4: This is an amazing and comforting promise. Gates are fixed defensive armaments. When Jesus says that the *gates of hell shall not prevail*, He is painting the picture of a conquering army that knocks down the gates and captures the city!

column4: The Holy Spirit brings supernatural boldness to proclaim the witness of the Gospel in the face of persecution. The outcome of this empowerment can be described, but it's best experienced. It’s a supernatural (greater than human) boldness that motivates believers to share. This boldness of preaching is often accompanied by supernatural acts of demonstration of the Spirit and of power (1 Corinthians 2:1-5). People are healed physically and emotionally, the dead raised, those tormented by evil spirits are set free, people with hard hearts turn and repent.
column5: The Holy Spirit brings miraculous boldness to proclaim the testimony of the Gospel in the face of persecution. The results of this empowerment can be described, but are far better to be lived. It is a miraculous boldness (greater than human) that emboldens believers to share. This boldness to preach is often accompanied by miraculous acts that demonstrate the Spirit and power (1 Corinthians 2:1-5). People are healed physically and emotionally, the dead are raised, those tormented by evil spirits are set free, people with hard hearts turn and repent.

column4: The Holy Spirit is the Helper. The Helper helps us! The work goes much more smoothly if we have a shared language, and relationship with Him. Can you imagine trying to work with someone in your job if you had no relationship, did not speak the same language, and couldn't communicate?!
column5: The Holy Spirit is a Helper. A Helper helps us! Work goes much more smoothly if we have a shared language, and a relationship with Him. Can you imagine trying to work with someone at your job if you have no relationship, you don't speak the same language, and you can't communicate?!

column4: We serve a God who wants to communicate with us. Jesus said that His sheep know His voice (John 10:27), we have built into us all already the natural abilities we need, but we may lack experienced proficiency.
column5: We serve a God who wants to communicate with us. Jesus said that His sheep know His voice (John 10:27), already within all of us we have been given the natural capacity we need, but we may lack the skill that comes from experience.

column4: Speaking from personal experience, a personal and active relationship with the Holy Spirit is one of the best things about being a Christian. His presence brings us peace, comfort, and direction, but only if you know how to seek, listen, and obey Him.
column5: Speaking from personal experience, a personal and living relationship with the Holy Spirit is one of the best things about being a Christian. His presence brings us peace, comfort, and direction, but only if you know how to seek Him, listen to Him, and obey Him.

column4: Develop a sensitivity with the Holy Spirit. Like many married people over time, you can communicate with your spouse in a unique way and sometimes just through a look. The look alone tells you everything you need to know about what just happened and what's going to happen. Build that type of sensitivity and familiarity with the Holy Spirit. Include Him in your whole life, this is a wonderful part of your relationship with Him that will provide so much depth and richness to your walk of faith.

Include Him in your whole life, this is a wonderful part of your relationship with Him that will bring great depth and richness to your walk of faith.

column4: The Holy Spirit has come to lead us and guide us, to empower us to be God’s people, and to see the people of the Earth radically transformed, delivered from the kingdom of darkness into the kingdom of light. Getting to know him, building trust with Him is essential to everyday life and to accomplish the work that Jesus has for us to do.
